content:
After months of testing, macOS 27 Golden Gate is now officially rolling out to all users, bringing a refreshed Siri AI, deeper Liquid Glass refinements, a number of major new Safari features, and a series of performance and user experience improvements. Here's everything you need to know about this update.

At this year's WWDC, Apple took a slightly different approach to introducing its operating systems.

Instead of walking through each platform one by one, Apple shortened the individual OS presentations and shifted the focus to cross-platform features and improvements — largely because many of the features depend on the new Apple Intelligence framework.

That said, macOS 27 Golden Gate still packs plenty of thoughtful design and feature refinements, starting with a series of Liquid Glass adjustments.

Liquid Glass and interface improvements

While macOS Tahoe 26 adopted Apple's new design language, it still fell a bit short visually — especially compared with iOS 26 and iPadOS 26.

In macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has spent more time further weaving the new Liquid Glass throughout the system, while also bringing in some of the visual tweaks from iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 — including a new Liquid Glass slider that lets users adjust the transparency effect themselves.

Tucked inside the Liquid Glass appearance settings is a fun Easter egg: Clarus the Dogcow — you'll find him if you scroll the demo panel all the way to the bottom.

macOS 27 Golden Gate has also redesigned app icons, adding an extra layer to bring deeper detail to the look of the system worldwide, spanning light, dark, tinted, and clear styles.

The red, yellow, and green traffic-light buttons introduced mid-beta have also been updated. The previously flat green, yellow, and red controls now sport a Liquid Glass look, and feature a cute bounce effect when the user clicks (or taps?) and drags before releasing.

Another thoughtful interface change in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Apple's decision to unify window and application corner radii across the system, rather than dynamically adjusting them based on the UI elements inside the window's menu bar.

Although Apple's choice was deliberate, many people mistook the inconsistent corner radii for a bug, prompting Apple to single out the change during the WWDC keynote.

Another controversial design decision involved icons. macOS 26 Tahoe added a symbol next to nearly every menu command, ostensibly to make menus easier to scan, but it was widely panned for making the interface more cluttered — and sometimes harder to scan.

Fortunately, in macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has reversed course, removing most of those icons and restoring a cleaner, more minimal look to the menus.

Other visual refinements in macOS 27 Golden Gate include edge-to-edge sidebars and a clearer distinction for the currently active window — both of which were points of contention during macOS Tahoe 26.

Siri AI and the new Siri app

This may well be the most important new feature in macOS 27 Golden Gate. The new Siri is co-developed with Google's Gemini model, has its own dedicated app, and is deeply integrated into the system.

The new Siri AI uses a new on-device index system to handle user data, and exists in both Spotlight and the new Siri app.

The new Siri app looks and behaves much like other AI assistant apps: a list of conversations across supported platforms on the left, the main chat panel in the middle where you can type a prompt, attach images or files, or start a conversation by voice. The app also supports searching and pinning conversations — a plus for users juggling multiple workflows.

The new Siri AI can pull information from the web and from a user's personal data to deliver actionable answers. During testing, reactions to the new Siri were generally positive, though it was occasionally a touch slower than other LLM AI assistants users expected.

Another practical capability of the new Siri AI is that it can interact with native and third-party apps and carry out actions directly — a significant improvement over the old Siri's app integration.

Developers need to expose their apps' content and capabilities through the App Intents framework, so as more developers update their apps for macOS 27 Golden Gate, this area is expected to keep getting better.

Finally, the system has added a universal "Ask Siri" right-click menu option that lets users select text, an image, or a file and query Siri about it directly. For example, you can Control-click an image in a document to ask Siri for more information; or select a passage of text and ask Siri to rewrite, proofread, adjust the tone, or suggest writing improvements.

Siri AI launches supporting English, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish arriving in October. Due to regulatory reasons, Siri AI is currently unavailable in mainland China and the European Union.

Apple Intelligence

We've covered Apple's new foundation models in detail before. In short, for its 2027 OS releases, Apple has developed a new generation of Apple Intelligence models. Here are Apple's official descriptions of each model:

AFM 3 Core, the next generation of our 3-billion-parameter dense model, with further quality improvements. AFM 3 Core Advanced, our most powerful on-device model, with native multimodal support, richer voice expression, and more accurate voice dictation. This 20-billion-parameter model is built on Apple's cutting-edge research and uses a sparse architecture that activates only 1 to 4 billion parameters as needed. AFM 3 Core Advanced requires and has been optimized for our most powerful Apple Silicon systems. AFM 3 Cloud, our server-side workhorse model, built for speed, efficiency, and capability. AFM 3 Cloud (Image), for image generation and editing, unlocking more advanced photo-editing tools, a new Image Playground, and more. AFM 3 Cloud Pro, our most powerful server-side model, powering the most demanding use cases, such as agentic tool use and complex reasoning.

In practice, macOS 27 Golden Gate uses two on-device models — AFM 3 Core and AFM 3 Core Advanced — with the rest running in the cloud. The performance of these two on-device models depends on the Mac's hardware, particularly the available memory, to handle their activation parameters and other AI workloads.

As for how Apple Intelligence actually performs on macOS 27 Golden Gate, the best word is mixed. The models themselves perform reasonably well on everyday tasks — helping draft emails, proofread documents, or summarise content, for example.

The problem is that Apple sometimes seems overly eager about how and when it surfaces Siri AI — sometimes annoying users and even getting in the way of what they're trying to do.

A standout new Apple Intelligence feature in macOS 27 Golden Gate is the new Visual Intelligence shortcut. Just press Command-Shift-Space and you can select any area on screen and query Siri about it right away — whether it's an image, a PDF, text, basically anything displayed on screen.

Unfortunately, not every Mac compatible with macOS 27 can run the new Apple Intelligence — it requires an A18 Pro, M1, or later chip. Here's the official list of supported newer Mac models Apple has published:

  • MacBook Neo (2026)
  • MacBook Air with Apple Silicon (2020 or later)
  • MacBook Pro with Apple Silicon (2020 or later)
  • iMac with Apple Silicon (2021 or later)
  • Mac mini with Apple Silicon (2020 or later)
  • Mac Studio (2022 or later)
  • Mac Pro with Apple Silicon (2023)

Most Apple Intelligence features support the languages Apple Intelligence has already offered, including Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

Due to regulatory reasons, Apple Intelligence is currently unavailable in mainland China. Apple has also noted that some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features will have usage limits, though the company hasn't released specific details yet.

Performance and stability improvements

During the WWDC26 keynote, Apple highlighted dozens of improvements spanning every operating system.

For macOS 27 Golden Gate, these include faster AirDrop transfers, improved network file browsing, faster Spotlight indexing (especially for shortcuts and actions), and faster iCloud Photos uploads with selective prioritisation.

macOS 27 Golden Gate has also improved scrolling performance in Safari and Calendar, as well as animation performance in Mission Control and Spaces. Apple has also tuned Mail's indexing and search, and the underlying system behind Spotlight suggestions.

Other improvements include more consistent and persistent window position memory on external displays, HDR support for system UI elements, broader support for high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes on external displays, and improved Sidecar touch support — including tap gestures, single-finger scrolling, system gestures, and markup.

Safari

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces a Safari feature called "Notify Me" that can monitor web pages and alert users when relevant changes appear — such as price drops, restocks, event registration opening, or anything else a user wants to track.

Notify Me can check every hour, day, week, or month, and you can also specify additional days and times for it to check.

In addition, Safari in macOS 27 Golden Gate gains a feature for "describing extensions" that lets users build extensions using natural language.

To help users get started, Apple provides several examples spanning productivity, focus, creative, and design/development categories. Users can also simply describe what they need in their own words and let Apple Intelligence handle the rest.

Both of these features are accessible from the "More Options" hamburger menu on the right side of existing tabs.

For users who like to keep a ton of tabs open, Safari can now automatically organise and group tabs by topic.

Another thoughtful touch in Safari on macOS 27 Golden Gate is the addition of a pull-to-refresh gesture similar to iOS and iPadOS, letting users swipe down with a "rubber band" effect to refresh the page.

This gesture also works in other system apps, such as Mail, News, and Calendar; many see it as another hint at the rumoured touchscreen Mac, which could be unveiled as soon as this year.

iPhone Mirroring

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, users can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window to different aspect ratios; many see this as an early sign that Apple is laying the groundwork for a foldable iPhone.

With the official launch of the iPhone Duo, Mac users can get an early taste. Unfortunately, Apple notes that iPhone Mirroring is still unavailable in the European Union.

Shortcuts

This feature is arguably one of the most useful Apple Intelligence additions in this year's OS updates.

Although Shortcuts is already a fairly approachable automation tool, it can still be intimidating for everyday users. Now, family users simply need to describe what they want to do, and Apple Intelligence will turn it into a native shortcut.

To help users get started, the Shortcuts app also highlights a number of suggestions at the top of the new shortcut creation screen, including:

  • Dictate and translate to Spanish
  • Write a haiku for the weather forecast
  • Play my workout playlist whenever I arrive at the gym
  • Make a dish with these leftovers
  • Summarise my day every morning
  • Prioritise my to-do list every morning
  • Give me driving directions as soon as I get in the car
  • Dictate my thoughts and save them to the clipboard
  • Dim the screen when it's bedtime
  • Turn on Do Not Disturb when the TV app opens

By the way, if you want to go deeper on Shortcuts, be sure to follow Stephen Robles on YouTube and Instagram. You can also check out Shortcuts Playground on MacStories, a more powerful natural-language shortcut builder.

Photos

The Photos app now offers three Apple Intelligence-powered editing tools: an enhanced Clean Up tool that can remove objects, people, or other unwanted elements from a photo; Extend, which can generate surrounding areas when you feel a shot was cropped too tightly; and Spatial Recompose, which lets you change the angle and composition of a photo after it's been taken.

In addition, iCloud Shared Albums now support full-resolution sharing and let you invite Windows and Android users to join via iicloud.com.

Other new features include the ability to play any set of photos and videos as a slideshow with music, transition effects, and playback time of your choice; a photo rating feature with a brand new star-rating system; and an all-new dedicated "Shot by Me" collection.

More macOS 27 Golden Gate details

  • Calendar lets users add, edit, or update events by describing them.
  • Finder can now intelligently suggest names based on the contents of files and folders.
  • Image Playground has expanded support for different styles and adopts a new foundation model for better results.
  • Maps' Flyover experience has been upgraded, bringing better textures, detail, and clarity to hundreds of cities worldwide.
  • Messages has finally (finally) integrated tap-back reaction notifications and improved cross-device sync performance.
  • Notes supports handwriting and drawing with the trackpad, expanded Markdown support, and adds copy/paste and section link features.
  • Podcasts now supports video podcasts, with picture-in-picture playback.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also marks the final version to support Rosetta. As Apple explains: "Only apps that have not been updated after installing this update will be unable to run on Macs with Apple Silicon" — you can learn more here.

Compatibility

According to Apple's official list, macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with the following Mac models:

  • MacBook Neo (2026)

What's your favourite new feature? Let us know in the comments.

Notable Amazon products

  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirTag (2nd generation) 4-pack
  • MacBook Neo
  • David Pogue — author of "Apple: The First 50 Years"
  • Logitech MX Master 4
  • Wireless CarPlay adapter
